name.text: Forming an inequality in two unknowns

questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(ix=1)"]]Kerubo has Ksh {@T@} to spend on \(x\) kg of tomatoes at Ksh {@p@} per kg and \(y\) packets of maize flour at Ksh {@q@} each.[[elif test="is(ix=2)"]]A school club sells \(x\) cups of tea at a profit of Ksh {@p@} each and \(y\) samosas at a profit of Ksh {@q@} each. It needs a profit of at least Ksh {@T@}.[[elif test="is(ix=3)"]]Mutua has Ksh {@T@} to spend on \(x\) litres of milk at Ksh {@p@} each and \(y\) loaves of bread at Ksh {@q@} each.[[elif test="is(ix=4)"]]A handcart must carry less than {@T@} kg. It carries \(x\) bags of {@p@} kg and \(y\) crates of {@q@} kg.[[elif test="is(ix=5)"]]At a charity walk in Eldoret, adults pay Ksh {@p@} and children pay Ksh {@q@}. The organisers need to collect more than Ksh {@T@}. \(x\) adults and \(y\) children take part.[[elif test="is(ix=6)"]]A matatu SACCO wants at least {@p@} times as many 14-seater matatus (\(x\)) as 33-seater buses (\(y\)).[[elif test="is(ix=7)"]]A kiosk makes a profit of Ksh {@p@} on each bottle of water (\(x\)) and Ksh {@q@} on each packet of groundnuts (\(y\)). The owner wants a profit of at least Ksh {@T@} in a week.[[elif test="is(ix=8)"]]Chebet has Ksh {@T@} to spend on \(x\) bars of soap at Ksh {@p@} each and \(y\) tubes of toothpaste at Ksh {@q@} each.[[elif test="is(ix=9)"]]A hotel buys at least {@p@} times as many cups (\(x\)) as teapots (\(y\)).[[else]]A tuk-tuk's load must be less than {@T@} kg. It carries \(x\) sacks of {@p@} kg and \(y\) trays of {@q@} kg.[[/if]]

(a) Write an inequality in \(x\) and \(y\).

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]If she buys {@x0@} kg of tomatoes, what is the greatest number of packets of maize flour she can buy?[[elif test="is(ix=2)"]]If the club sells {@x0@} cups of tea, what is the least number of samosas it must sell?[[elif test="is(ix=3)"]]If he buys {@x0@} litres of milk, what is the greatest number of loaves he can buy?[[elif test="is(ix=4)"]]If it carries {@x0@} bags, what is the greatest number of crates it can carry?[[elif test="is(ix=5)"]]If {@x0@} adults take part, what is the least number of children needed?[[elif test="is(ix=6)"]]If the SACCO has {@x0@} buses, what is the least number of matatus it needs?[[elif test="is(ix=7)"]]If the kiosk sells {@x0@} bottles of water, what is the least number of packets of groundnuts it must sell?[[elif test="is(ix=8)"]]If she buys {@x0@} bars of soap, what is the greatest number of tubes of toothpaste she can buy?[[elif test="is(ix=9)"]]If it buys {@x0@} teapots, what is the least number of cups?[[else]]If it carries {@x0@} sacks, what is the greatest number of trays it can carry?[[/if]]

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) [[if test="tms"]]At least {@p@} times as many \(x\) as \(y\) means \(x\) is at least {@p@} lots of \(y\): {@ansd@}. Check with \(y = 1\): \(x\) must be at least \({@p@}\).[[else]]The total {@totw@} is \({@p@}x + {@q@}y\), and it must be {@wd@} \({@T@}\): {@ansd@}.[[/if]]

(b) [[if test="tms"]]Put \(y = {@x0@}\): \(x \ge {@p*x0@}\), so the least number is \({@ansb@}\).[[else]]Put \(x = {@x0@}\): \({@p*x0@} + {@q@}y {@relt(rel)@} {@T@}\), so \({@q@}y {@relt(rel)@} {@T-p*x0@}\) and \(y {@relt(rel)@} {@nd(bv)@}\). \(y\) must be a whole number, so the answer is \({@ansb@}\).[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: forming an inequality in two unknowns

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Form a linear inequality in two unknowns from a budget, a target, a load or a ratio, and use it.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 1 (Graphing inequalities), Section C, question C7 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new Kenyan contexts and numbers, with budgets, targets, loads and ratios.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: [[if test="tms"]]Test your inequality with numbers that fit the sentence: \(x = {@p@}\) and \(y = 1\). Yours says \(1 \ge {@p*p@}\), which is false. Which letter stands for the bigger number?[[else]]You matched the numbers to the wrong letters: \(x\) goes with \({@p@}\) and \(y\) goes with \({@q@}\).[[/if]]

[[if test="tms"]]Your sign points the wrong way: your inequality allows \(x = 0\) with \(y = 1\). Does that fit at least {@p@} times as many?[[else]]Your sign points the wrong way: the total must be {@wd@} \({@T@}\).[[/if]]

[[if test="tms"]]At least includes \(x = {@p@}y\) itself, so use \(\ge\).[[elif test="strictp(rel)"]]{@wd@} does not include \({@T@}\) itself, so use a strict sign.[[else]]{@wd@} includes \({@T@}\) itself, so use \(\le\) or \(\ge\).[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="tms"]]Compare \(x\) with {@p@} lots of \(y\). Check with \(y = 1\): \(x\) must be at least \({@p@}\).[[else]]Write the total {@totw@} as \(({@p@} \times x) + ({@q@} \times y)\), then compare it with \({@T@}\) using the words of the question.[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: [[if test="tms"]]\(x = {@wb@}\) is allowed, but is it the least? Try one fewer in your inequality: at least includes equal.[[elif test="is(kind=\"budget\")"]]Round down: \({@wb@}\) would cost \({@p*x0+q*wb@}\) shillings, more than Ksh {@T@}.[[elif test="is(kind=\"target\")"]]Round up: with \({@wb@}\) the profit is \({@p*x0+q*wb@}\) shillings, less than Ksh {@T@}.[[elif test="is(kind=\"cart\")"]]With \({@wb@}\) the total is exactly \({@T@}\) kg, which is not less than \({@T@}\) kg.[[else]]With \({@wb@}\) the total is exactly Ksh {@T@}, which is not more than Ksh {@T@}.[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="not b2i"]]The answer must be a whole number. [[elif test="tms and b2ok"]]\(x = {@ans2@}\) is allowed, but it is not the least number that is. [[elif test="tms"]]With \(y = {@x0@}\), \(x = {@ans2@}\) is too few: it is less than \({@p@}\) times \({@x0@}\). [[elif test="b2ok"]]With \(x = {@x0@}\) and \(y = {@ans2@}\) the {@totw@} would be \({@b2t@}\), which is allowed, but \({@ans2@}\) is not the [[if test="upper"]]greatest[[else]]least[[/if]] number that is. [[else]]With \(x = {@x0@}\) and \(y = {@ans2@}\) the {@totw@} would be \({@b2t@}\), which is [[if test="upper"]]more[[else]]less[[/if]] than \({@T@}\). [[/if]][[if test="tms"]]Put \(y = {@x0@}\) into your inequality and find the least whole number \(x\) that makes it true.[[else]]Put \(x = {@x0@}\) into your inequality and find the [[if test="upper"]]greatest[[else]]least[[/if]] whole number \(y\) that makes it true. Check the next whole number as well.[[/if]]
